newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk warplanes bomb Kurd rebel camps in north Iraq.
newsitem.headline: Turk warplanes bomb Kurd rebel camps in north Iraq.

text.p: Turkish warplanes bombed Kurdish guerrilla camps in northern Iraq as ground forces continued a cross-border operation against rebels in the region, state-run Anatolian news agency said on Wednesday.

The F-4 fighter-bombers took off from the southeastern Turkish city of Diyarbakir and destroyed three camps of the rebel Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK) in the Sinath region of northern Iraq, the agency said, quoting military sources.
The emergency rule governor's office in Diyarbakir said 75 Kurdish rebels and two soldiers had been killed in the operation since it began on Monday night.
It said the operation was continuing on Wednesday.
Anatolian said Cobra helicopters launched bomb attacks on other PKK guerrillas trying to escape across the border into Iraq.
The operation began after PKK rebels in Iraq had fired on troops along the border near the southeastern Turkish town of Silopi, Anatolian said.
The Turkish armed forces responded by crossing the border near Silopi in brigade strength, together with air support.
More than 21,000 people have been killed in the 12-year-old conflict between the security forces and the PKK who are fighting for self-rule in Turkey's mainly Kurdish southeast.
